observations: Vintage mechanical or electromechanical adding machine with a numeric keypad.
A paper roll is mounted at the rear for printing.
A manual crank handle is attached to the right side.
A metal plate on the top casing reads 'TRS 108'.
The front casing has 'PAN' written on it in black marker.
The rear identification plate says 'MADE IN SINGAPORE' but the fields for Voltage (V) and Frequency (Hz) are blank.
The keypad includes digits 0-9 and several function keys (#, *, diamond, minus).
The plastic casing shows significant yellowing and age-related wear.

claims.evidence: The printing mechanism is visible but its technology (dot matrix vs impact wheel) cannot be confirmed from photos.
The device is a numeric adding machine/calculator, not a typewriter for text entry.

risks.risk: Mechanical seizure or internal damage to the crank and calculation gears.
risks.proof: A video showing the handle being turned and the machine completing a cycle.

risks.risk: Printing mechanism failure or dried/proprietary ink ribbon that is no longer available.
risks.proof: A photo of a fresh printout on the paper roll.

risks.risk: Missing internal components or heavy internal corrosion.
risks.proof: Photos of the internal mechanism with the top cover removed.

proof_requests: A video of the machine in operation, showing the keys being pressed and the crank handle being turned.
A photo of a recent calculation printed on the paper tape.
A photo of the bottom of the unit to check for a battery compartment or power cord entry.
response.reason: The item is a vintage TRS 108 adding machine. Due to its age and the lack of functional proof, it is priced at its worst case as a non-working decorative or parts-only item.
